CHIEF COMPLAINT
Asthma affecting sports participation and mood concerns

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient reports asthma and attempted to join water polo team. Experiencing difficulty breathing during sports and aerobic activities. Describes symptoms of phlegm buildup in throat, cough, chest tightness, wheezing, and lightheadedness during exertion. Currently using albuterol inhaler 2 puffs as needed for acute symptoms. Reports albuterol helps with phlegm but still requires sitting down to recover, with improvement within about 15 minutes. Experiences shaking after using inhaler, which was confirmed as expected side effect. Has symptoms with almost every aerobic workout. Denies nocturnal asthma symptoms. Also reports cough when around smoke but typically avoids smokers. Has not tried daily asthma medications, only uses rescue inhaler during acute attacks.

Patient also reports mood concerns that started this year. Describes stress related to SATs, AP classes, and school pressure. Reports sadness, lack of motivation, fatigue, and prefers to stay home rather than go out with friends. Initially tried sports hoping to feel more energized and happy but mood has worsened.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Seasonal allergies confirmed. Cough with smoke exposure. No other systems reviewed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

MEDICATIONS
Albuterol inhaler PRN (2 puffs)

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
High school student taking AP classes and studying for SATs. Wants to participate in water polo. Socializes with friends.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
HEENT: Eyes okay. Fluid noted in ears. Mouth and throat fine, no tonsils noted.
Cardiovascular: Heart sounds good.

Not discussed.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Asthma: Start Singulair daily medication. Continue albuterol inhaler as needed for acute symptoms. Counseled on expected side effects of albuterol; advised to sit down after use. Expect to see improvement within about one month. Follow-up in 6 weeks.
Mood: Refer to therapist. Screening questionnaires to be completed. Follow-up in couple of weeks.
